messages:
miriam: saw an unexpected provisional vs confirmed delta for a streaming session that fell back mid-stream.

sam: can you paste the provisional lines you saw?

miriam: pasted below (redacted ids):
```
SESSION id=sess-9c3e
ROUTE primary gpu-a cost=0.0036/token
ROUTE fallback cpu-b cost=0.0008/token
STREAM prefix billed 430 tokens
FALLBACK when gpu unavailable -> start new provisional range
RESUME after fallback -> billed resume 140 tokens
TOOLCALL client-side truncation -> billed 90 tokens
PROVISIONAL_SUM = 660 tokens
CONFIRMED_SUM  = 560 tokens
```

alex: looks like overlap de-dup didn't run when we stitched ranges across route boundaries. we end up double-counting prefix tokens that were owned provisionally by primary and then reissued on fallback.

miriam: note: truncation creates a toolcall entry that's keyed to the active route. when route flips we currently generate a new toolcall provisional and later the finalizer merges by timestamp, but we don't dedupe toolcall ids across routes.

sam: is this purely an accounting visibility problem or can it push customers over per-route quotas?

alex: both. quotas are enforced against provisional totals during the session until finalization. that means a customer can be throttled on the primary route because provisional_total > quota even though confirmed will be lower after dedupe.

jess: product wants a short-term UX mitigation. can we surface provisional vs confirmed delta in the console per-route and per-session? add a tooltip: "final counts published after session reconciliation" and a small badge if delta > 5%.

miriam: implementation plan suggestion: 1) keep fast provisional snapshots for low-latency metrics, 2) tag provisional ranges with transient ownership metadata on handoff, 3) finalization pass runs a merge+dedupe across route ranges and toolcall ids before emitting confirmed ledger.

alex: algorithm caveat: we must be careful with resume ordering — clients can resume at a sequence that overlaps a previously owned prefix. merge-pass must operate on sequence ranges, not just token counts, and reconcile toolcall ids (global dedupe set keyed by client session + toolcall-hash).

sam: i'll add prometheus counters: redwood.session.provisional_tokens, redwood.session.confirmed_tokens, redwood.session.deduped_tokens. also a gauge for redwood.route.provisional_delta_pct. i'll wire a dashboard tile showing provisional vs confirmed and a heatmap for routes with high deltas.

miriam: i'll write unit tests for: overlapping range dedupe, toolcall dedupe across handoffs, and resume+truncation ordering. will pair on the merge-pass tomorrow morning 10:30am PT.

alex: operational note: until this is fixed, we'll mark affected customers as "provisional-sensitive" and avoid hard quota-enforcement on provisional totals for >=30min after finalization. ops, please do a communication to billing if any customers see >10% provisional deltas.

billing-bot: Incident #2026-214 created: provisional-ledger-delta > 5% detected for acct-642. Billing alerted.

sam: i'll open a small PR for the metrics + dashboard tile and a follow-up PR for merge-pass. want to canary merge to a small subset of routes (10% of traffic) after unit tests pass.

jess: SG. UX will show the badge + tooltip. we'll include a short explainer in release notes about provisional vs confirmed counts during rollouts.

miriam: thanks. pairing tomorrow and i'll attach test vectors from the problematic session so we can reproduce.

alex: good plan. once we have dedupe in finalizer and the dashboard signal we can remove the provisional soft-quota hold and do a staged rollout.

sam: ping #release-war-room when the PR is ready for canary.
